items.title: From connected customers to flexible homes: How Tibber and Enode are shaping the open energy ecosystem for the next grid
items.summary: For most of the power system's history, flexibility came from large industrial assets. That is changing. Electric vehicles, home batteries, solar panels, heat pumps and chargers are bringing flexibility into millions of homes. As these technologies become more common, households are becoming active participants in the energy system. The challenge is no longer simply supplying electricity. It is helping customers optimize how they use it, while building the foundation for a more flexible energy system. Unlocking flexibility requires more than connected devices. It requires connected homes, interoperable ecosystems and the ability to coordinate assets as part of a system. For Tibber, connected devices help customers save money, earn rewards, and get more value from the technologies they already own. For Enode, they are the foundation for residential energy flexibility. Together, Tibber and Enode are helping build a future where homes are not only consumers of electricity, but active participants in the next grid.

items.title: SMA partners with Enode to unlock solar and battery flexibility for the next grid
items.summary: SMA, a leading provider of solar solutions, partners with Enode to help energy companies connect and optimize SMA assets through a single, reliable integration. As households adopt more distributed energy resources, including solar panels, home batteries, electric vehicles and heat pumps, energy companies need reliable ways to connect these assets and deliver seamless customer experiences. Through this partnership, energy retailers, utilities and energy platforms using Enode, can integrate SMA-connected assets into energy products and flexibility programs without building and maintaining their own integration.

items.title: Introducing asset overview: Find the right assets in seconds, not days
items.summary: Once your asset base grows, finding the right assets to investigate becomes hard. A customer asked us a simple question: “Can I get a list of all BMW vehicles with an active intervention? We want to reach out to those users directly.” It sounds straightforward. But getting to that list meant either querying the data internally or asking our support team to pull it and export it. What should have taken ten seconds took days of back-and-forth. Asset overview is built for this exact moment.

items.title: Ostrom connects tens of thousands of devices across a growing energy ecosystem
items.summary: Connected, flexible energy systems depend on interoperability between retailers, hardware manufacturers, and the partners that orchestrate them. Each plays a role in making these products work. Ostrom brings these pieces together at scale through its dynamic tariff and NeoGrid VPP, connecting devices directly into the core energy product. Over the past year, the company has nearly doubled its connected device base to tens of thousands of electrical vehicle (EV) chargers, batteries, and solar systems. Battery connections alone have grown by around 200 percent year over year. As Ostrom expands its connected offering, partners like go-e are seeing equally impressive growth, with their devices reaching more engaged customers through the ecosystem.

items.title: Indra and Enode partner to bring smart EV charging into energy apps and flexibility programs
items.summary: Indra Renewable Technologies, a UK-based smart energy technology company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Malvern, Worcestershire, is working with Enode to make its chargers available within the energy apps and services that retailers offer to their customers. The company specializes in intelligent EV charging and has been an early driver of bidirectional charging, showing how EVs can support both households and the wider energy system. Through this partnership, Indra chargers can be connected into energy apps and flexibility programs powered by Enode. This allows Indra owners to connect their chargers to their energy provider’s app and access smart charging features without any additional setup.

items.title: Set Charge Rate Limit: Control EV charging in kW
items.summary: The most valuable EV charging optimizations don't just manage when charging occurs, they also control how fast an EV charges. Set Charge Rate Limit is in Beta and available for the following charger brands: ChargeAmps, Easee, Garo, go-e, Keba, and Zaptec. Full Sandbox support and a Dashboard Asset View are also included. Support for additional charger brands is being added over time. If your users have linked a vehicle and charger, you'll be able to control the charge rate via the Vehicle API.

items.title: Q1 recap: Scaling flexibility across the ecosystem
items.summary: If Q4 was about launching Flex, Q1 has been about scaling with customers and partners. As more energy retailers move from early pilots to operational programs, the focus is shifting. It is less about whether flexibility works, and more about how to run programs reliably across growing portfolios of devices and markets. This quarter reflects that shift.

items.title: Peblar x Enode: Expanding EV charger choices for energy retailers
items.summary: Across the Netherlands, electric vehicle (EV) adoption is moving from early growth to mainstream. For energy retailers, that shift is changing what customers expect from their energy provider. What began as EV-specific tariffs is evolving into offers that include a home charger, app-based smart charging, and flexibility programs designed to optimize renewable energy use and support grid stability. Now, EV charging optimization is becoming part of the core energy proposition, not an add-on. As expectations rise, EV charging needs to be reliable, easy to manage in the same app customers already use for their energy management, and delivered as part of a cohesive customer experience. That is why we are partnering with Peblar.

items.title: Enode selected by ENGIE to scale residential EV flexibility
items.summary: ENGIE, a global energy player serving 19 million residential contracts worldwide, is partnering with Enode to scale residential flexibility for its energy retail portfolio in Belgium, France and the Netherlands. As electrification accelerates and more customers adopt electrical vehicles (EVs), home chargers, and other home energy technologies, consumer flexibility is becoming a strategic lever to both improve the customer proposition and unlock new operational value. This partnership reflects a broader shift across European energy retail. Consumer flexibility is becoming a core capability, not an experiment, and requires platforms built for reliability, governance, and growth.

items.title: Enode x SAP: SAP has chosen Enode to enable residential flexibility within SAP Distributed Energy Resources
items.summary: Energy retailers are moving from experimentation to long-term decisions about residential flexibility. Today, flexibility needs to operate as part of day-to-day business, not as a side initiative. SAP sees that shift clearly. That’s why SAP has chosen Enode to enable SAP Distributed Energy Resources, a solution supporting residential distributed energy resource (DER) flexibility within SAP environments. The partnership brings Enode’s full product capabilities into the SAP ecosystem, allowing utilities to manage residential flexibility with the same operational discipline they apply to the rest of their business.

items.title: High-resolution vehicle images now in Enode API | Enode
items.summary: The Enode API now includes an imageUrl field for every supported vehicle model — studio-quality images served via CDN with flexible sizing, format, and compression options.

items.title: Energy Retail in 2026: Trends That Will Define the Year
items.summary: Energy retail is entering a phase where long-term decisions start to take hold. Across Europe, retailers face the same underlying tension. Customer expectations are rising, market shares are becoming more fluid, and value is increasingly tied to how well consumption can be steered, not just supplied. Based on what we see across markets, customers, and partners, we have identified five trends that will shape how energy retail evolves in the year ahead.

items.title: EnBW x Enode: Making home energy management simple for every household
items.summary: Home energy is changing fast. As the economy electrifies, rising electricity demand from EVs, heat pumps and other connected devices, puts more pressure on the grid. At the same time, these devices are increasingly smart and controllable. EnBW set out to simplify energy by focusing on four core capabilities: seamless connectivity, clear visualization, intelligent optimization and control when it’s needed. That vision comes to life in EnBW Mavi, EnBW’s home energy experience that brings e-mobility both at home and away from home, local consumption and generation, and cost transparency together in one place. The guiding principle is simple: provide customers with full transparency and control over their energy consumption, as simply for them as possible.

items.title: myenergi x Enode: How EV charging is shifting from hardware to flexibility
items.summary: Over the past decade, electric mobility has gone from niche to mainstream. Millions of drivers have made the switch to electric, supported by an expanding network of home chargers that make charging simple and convenient. But as adoption accelerates, something new is happening. The focus is shifting from access to intelligence. We spoke with our partner, myenergi, about how the EV charging industry has evolved, and how collaboration with Enode is shaping what comes next.

items.title: Looking back at 2025 at Enode
items.summary: 2025 was a big year for Enode. We partnered with more OEMs and energy companies than ever before. Customers launched services that are now live with millions of users. We shipped major new products. The team grew. And in November, we passed 500,000 connected energy devices on the platform. What matters most to us is how these things connect. Each partnership, product launch, and customer rollout moved us closer to the same goal we’ve been working toward from the start: making energy systems easier to build, easier to scale, and ready for flexibility.

items.title: Sungrow and Enode partner to make smart energy management more accessible
items.summary: Sungrow is a global leader in solar and storage energy solutions, powering millions of homes with reliable, high-performance devices that produce clean energy. Now, together with Enode, they’re making it easier for households everywhere to connect, optimize, and take control of their energy. Through this partnership, Sungrow enables customers to connect their solar and storage devices to their preferred energy management apps. This gives them access to competitive tariffs and smart features that help optimize energy use and lower bills.

items.title: Essent: Making smart charging work for everyone
items.summary: The Netherlands is one of Europe’s fastest-growing EV markets. Over 35% of new vehicles are now electric, and most charging happens at home. This convenience is also a challenge: unmanaged home charging can increase peak electricity demand, driving higher costs across the grid. For Essent, this is more than a technical grid issue, it’s a once-in-a-decade customer opportunity. Whoever makes smart charging effortless for mainstream consumers will shape the next decade of residential energy. Partnering with Enode gave Essent seamless access to over 60 EV and charger brands, allowing its teams to focus on proposition design and the customer experience instead of managing API integrations.

items.title: Meet Enode Flex: the flexibility platform for energy retailers
items.summary: When we started Enode, we believed that connecting and optimising energy devices could meaningfully improve how the energy system works. Retailers have connected thousands of devices through Enode, but turning that potential into real flexibility has been a challenge. Flex changes that by giving teams one place to understand, shape and operate their flexible load. It’s a practical step toward using everyday devices to support a renewable grid.

items.title: Behind the Circuit: Meet Julien Rizzo, Senior Product Manager
items.summary: Product at Enode sits at the centre of how we build. It’s about understanding complex systems, solving hard problems with clarity and making things feel simple for the people who use our platform. In this edition of Behind the Circuit, we speak with Julien Rizzo, Senior Product Manager for EV charging, about his path from fintech to energy, why the connectivity layer is so important and how he thinks about building both products and processes that last.

items.title: Enode and BMW Group partner to unlock smarter, more connected charging for European drivers
items.summary: Enode and BMW Group have entered a partnership to enable a fully supported integration for BMW and MINI vehicles. The collaboration enables a high-quality, reliable connection that gives drivers access to the energy apps and services they rely on to manage charging and make the most of renewable energy.

items.title: The EU Data Act: what it means for the energy industry
items.summary: On September 12, 2025, the EU Data Act became fully applicable across the EU. Over the past weeks, we’ve explored the regulation in detail: what it covers, what it means in practice, and how energy companies can go beyond compliance to create real value. Now we’ve brought those insights together into one comprehensive report: The EU Data Act: what it means for the energy industry.

items.title: How PV inverter and battery manufacturers can unlock growth across Europe
items.summary: Europe’s solar and storage market is entering a new phase. Growth is spreading across more countries, and consumers are demanding more than efficient hardware. Home Energy Management (HEM) apps are becoming decisive in consumer choice. Our latest whitepaper explores how manufacturers can succeed in this new landscape. It looks at the strategies they are considering and shares new survey insights from leading manufacturers, including why 90% see HEM apps as essential to future sales and why most believe their own apps still fall short today.

items.title: Beyond compliance: How manufacturers can win with the EU Data Act
items.summary: Today, the EU Data Act becomes fully applicable across the EU. For device manufacturers, energy apps and aggregators, this marks a significant milestone. The past few years have been about preparing. From today, the focus shifts to doing: making device data open and portable, enabling user choice, and creating services that thrive in an open ecosystem. The companies that see this as more than compliance will be the ones that win.

items.title: ev.energy and Enode are building an interoperable ecosystem to unlock flexibility for every EV driver
items.summary: We’re partnering with ev.energy, a global leader in smart EV charging services, to unlock the full potential of energy flexibility for EVs and other DERs – making smart energy management available to all homes and drivers, regardless of their specific hardware or make. Our partnership underscores a shared vision: to build an open and scalable flexible energy landscape through a pragmatic and technology agnostic approach.

items.title: The EU Data Act in practice: What’s next for devices, apps, and users
items.summary: On September 12, 2025, the EU Data Act will become fully applicable across the EU. In our first blog we explained what the regulation is and why it matters for energy devices. This time, we’re looking ahead. What will actually change once the law takes effect? How will manufacturers, energy apps and aggregators, and end users experience the shift toward open energy data?

items.title: Resideo Grid Services and Enode expand access to residential energy flexibility
items.summary: Resideo Grid Services, a leading smart-home energy management provider in North America, and partner Enode will help utilities unlock more value from residential demand flexibility. The collaboration makes it easier to launch and scale programs that connect a wider range of home energy devices—including batteries, solar inverters, and EV chargers—while enabling homeowners to participate directly through their utility or energy provider’s existing platform. Together, Resideo Grid Services and Enode are making residential flexibility more accessible, impactful, and scalable than ever before.

items.title: How Sense is unlocking real-time energy insights for every home
items.summary: Sense is on a mission to make homes smarter and more energy aware. Their software, embedded in next-generation smart meters, translates raw electrical signals into real-time insights, helping consumers understand exactly how energy is being used in their home, device by device. Now, with the launch of EV Analytics, Sense is bringing that intelligence to one of the fastest-growing parts of the home: electric vehicles. EV Analytics helps households understand charging behavior, optimize costs, and prepare for the future of smart charging. To make it possible, Sense partnered with Enode.

items.title: Fuse Energy delivers super cheap EV charging with Enode
items.summary: Fuse is the fastest growing energy retailer in the UK for a reason. They offer some of the most competitive fixed and time-of-use (ToU) tariffs on the market, alongside a seamless switching experience through the Fuse app and web. Now, Fuse is partnering with Enode to take that experience even further, bringing intelligent EV charging and public charging features to EV owners across the UK.

items.title: Iberdrola uses Enode to connect millions to a smarter energy system
items.summary: Iberdrola has long been a frontrunner in clean energy, with one of the world’s largest renewable generation portfolios and a commitment to electrifying society through innovation across the entire energy value chain. As Iberdrola looked to scale, it became clear that hardware alone wasn’t enough. That shift brought Enode into the picture.

items.title: How Eneco is realizing their vision for a residential VPP offering with Enode
items.summary: Eneco is an international energy company serving millions of residential customers across the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany. With sustainability at the core of their mission, they are already a market leader in virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities, operating large-scale assets like wind farms, solar parks, and commercial batteries. Now, with the rapid growth of residential distributed energy resources (DERs) – the EV market alone is set to double in the Netherlands and Belgium by 2029 – Eneco is preparing to extend their VPP to the home. Their goal: empower consumers to better manage their energy use, contribute to grid stability, and offer possibilities to lower their energy bills. To help unlock this opportunity, Eneco partnered with Enode.

items.title: How Pod Point and Enode are enabling wholesale EV flexibility
items.summary: Pod Point, one of the UK’s leading EV charging providers, recently entered a new energy flex market, becoming the first company to sell energy in the wholesale market under the new P415 regulations. By partnering with Enode, Pod Point is progressing its Energy Flex strategy; helping customers charge their EVs at the most cost-effective times while supporting the Grid with demand-balancing.

items.title: Clever and Enode partner to build state-of-the-art smart charging with real-time EV data
items.summary: Clever's connects directly to EVs via Enode’s API to access real time state of charge and charge rate data, and make smart charging even smarter.

items.title: Vattenfall and Enode bring smart charging to EV owners in Sweden
items.summary: Vattenfall is making it easier for EV owners in Sweden to optimize their energy use with smart charging powered by Enode.

items.title: Softcom and Enode join forces to accelerate the energy transition for grid operators
items.summary: Operating the energy grid is more complex than ever. With rising renewables and the urgent need for flexibility, DSOs need smarter solutions to balance supply and demand. Our partnership with Softcom empowers DSOs to manage evolving grid challenges today — and future-proof their operations for tomorrow.

items.title: The blueprint for building consumer flexibility solutions
items.summary: Strong consumer flexibility products can elevate energy suppliers' offering, and presents a growing opportunity to engage consumers, lower energy costs and reduce pressure on the grid. But building them is challenging, and navigating the complexities can slow time to market. That’s why we created a new guide with insights and practical advice on how to frame your thinking around flexibility.

items.title: NeoCharge and Enode partner to help EV drivers in the US get more value from their vehicles
items.summary: NeoCharge is accelerating the transition to an all-electric future by making EV charging and home electrification more accessible. We're excited to collaborate with them to help make this happen, and on even more innovative use cases as NeoCharge makes strides into the US home energy management space.

items.title: How Kraken’s energy flexibility platform is maximizing market reach
items.summary: Learn more about how Kraken is helping the world’s largest energy companies manage and optimize distributed energy resources (DERs) in real-time and at scale, and why they’ve partnered with Enode to help maximize reach.

items.title: How to connect DERMS platforms to home batteries and capture the market
items.summary: The growing home battery market presents a massive opportunity. We've put together a guide on how DERMS providers can work with home batteries to make them less taxing on the grid, and more valuable to consumers.

items.title: How Synergi is accelerating product development and empowering more energy consumers using Enode
items.summary: Finland-based energy management solution Synergi wants to make it easy for consumers to save on their energy bills and positively contribute to the energy transition by using electricity flexibly. To maximize impact, they wanted to offer a range of consumption management services supporting all types of residential energy devices. Here's how partnering with Enode enabled them to do that without tying up too much time or development resources.

items.title: How EDP is building a home energy super-app with Enode’s EV API
items.summary: To unlock more value for their customers, EDP wanted to enable new home energy management use cases in their Solar app. Here's how they are taking the app one step further by partnering with Enode.

items.title: How Ostrom built a powerful, all-in-one home energy management app using Enode
items.summary: Find out how Ostrom is leading a change in the German energy market – and how they built a beloved home energy management app. Here's how they're helping customers easily track and flexibly manage energy consumption by partnering with Enode.

items.title: The beginner's guide to EV data
items.summary: Want an overview of how EV data can be accessed, what kind of data is available via EV APIs and what value-adding solutions they can help build? Then we have just the guide for you.
